exposure: Maternal thyroid dysfunction (overt hypothyroidism, subclinical hyperthyroidism, overt hyperthyroidism)
outcome: Maternal outcomes (anaemia, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, mode of delivery, antepartum haemorrhage)
Perinatal outcomes (gestational age at delivery, birth weight, small for gestational age (SGA), large for gestational age (LGA), NICU admission, perinatal mortality)
cohort: The study included 313 pregnant women attending an antenatal clinic or admitted to the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Department over 18 months.
finding: Maternal thyroid dysfunction, particularly overt forms, was linked to a higher incidence of adverse maternal (gestational diabetes mellitus, antepartum haemorrhage) and perinatal (low birth weight, SGA infants, NICU admissions, perinatal mortality) outcomes.
